utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please sit down. If I could remind you of the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence; that still applies. Mr. Khan has, I think, some more questions for you. Mr. Khan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: I'm grateful, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: I'll try not to be too long and I'll apologise at the outset for an irritating cough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I doubt we can hold you personally responsible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: I'm grateful. Your Honour, perhaps we can go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: We've agreed that when you were speaking to Mr. Black yesterday, you agreed with him yesterday that with regard to the statement you made in November when he asked you if you spoke the truth you said that you did. Now I'm going to move on to my next question, which is -- Mr. Black did not ask you those questions with regard to the statement that you made to the CCIU. So my first question to you is this, sir: When you made the statement to the CCIU before you made the statement to the investigator from the ICTY in November of 2002, did you - using Mr. Black's words - answer all the questions of your own free will?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The way it was I answered approximately with the CCIU. I know Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. that I mentioned those persons and where they took me. I mentioned this in CCIU as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry. That wasn't my question. And if you listen to my question and if you try to answer my question, then I won't have to ask it more than once. My question was: Did you answer the questions of your own free will when you spoke to the CCIU? It's a simple question and you can answer it yes or no because either you did or you didn't.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of my free will because of the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Excellent. Now, with regard to the other question that Mr. Black had asked you about the ICTY statement, I'm going to ask you that question also. When you spoke to the people at the CCIU, did you answer the questions truthfully, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave some names there. It was a shorter statement, and I said that maybe they will bring some news to us, but they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: You didn't answer my question, so I'm going to have to ask it again. Which is: When you spoke to the folks at the CCIU, did you answer their questions truthfully, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, I told them the truth. It was in the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you also had an opportunity to be involved in a discussion with Serbian authorities. And without talking about what happened there, I just want to establish that you were in a room with Serbian authorities in which there was a discussion about what happened to you. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About Lapusnik or where? What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Well, if I understand your testimony from yesterday when you were being asked questions by Mr. Black you were asked the following question - and I just want to make sure whether or not it's accurate or not. I'm trying to get some help here as I told you, I'm a little confused - Mr. Black asked you yesterday: "Witness, were you ever interviewed by the Serb authorities about your experiences in the summer of 1998?" And you responded: "They caught me in a village. It's not that I voluntarily gave information. They intercepted me in a village and took me into a police station." All I'm trying to do for the moment is establish whether or not that in fact is an accurate statement, that's what happened, that you were caught by the Serb authorities and you were taken to a police station.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Good.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Now, with regard to that incident, as I understand your testimony here, what you were interested in doing during that time was escaping. You wanted to get away from the Serb authorities; that's what you've told us. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how it was and I escaped.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: During the time that you were with the Serb authorities - and as you put it you were trying to escape - they asked you questions, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if they asked me questions. I know they asked me, Where have you been? I told them, I don't know where I've been because I was blindfolded. I don't know of giving them any other information. They asked me to come the following day and give a statement. And I said, Okay, I will come because there's no other place I can go to. And to my knowledge, I didn't say there that I saw any person at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Okay. I just asked you whether or not they asked you questions, and your answer was, and I'm going to quote your answer which was first of all: "I don't know if they asked me questions." And then you said: "I know they asked me, Where have you been." So in fact your answer would be: Yes, they asked me questions. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if they asked me questions. They did ask me questions, but I didn't say anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Okay. Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If we could go into private session for a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Are we in open session?

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Yesterday in response to a question asked of you by Mr. Black with regard to what you told the Serb authorities when they picked you up sometime in September or October of 1998 you said in response to the question: "Q. And what did you tell them? "A. I told them that I don't know where I was, that I have no idea. I just told them how it happened." And then you said, which is the part that I'd like to discuss with you: "They had all information." With regard to that statement that you made yesterday "they had all information," what information did they have that they discussed with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had information where I was staying. At that time I was staying in Ferizaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Apart from information of where you were staying, did they have any other information concerning Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They asked me, Where have you been? I told them that I didn't know, and I don't remember saying anything to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you gave a statement to the folks at the CCIU in August of 2001, did they come to you or did you go to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Before you went to them to make this statement, had you had some previous contact with them? Had you talked to some investigators either in person or on the phone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have such contacts. They had informed families at the Red Cross, and then I went to the CCIU and spoke to them. I didn't have any phone conversation with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Okay. And when you spoke with them, do you recall during the conversation that you had with them whether or not they told you that you had to provide your details correctly and to the best of your knowledge? Do you recall them making such a statement to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe they did. As I said, I had my interpreter. Maybe it wasn't interpreted correctly, and we couldn't trust everyone at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Now, the interpreter that you had with you on that day --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could we go into private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Well, it was actually the second time that you had given a statement. The first statement you gave was the reluctant statement to the Serb authorities where they questioned you. Here --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I see Mr. Black is rising.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I just think we should be careful. He didn't say he gave a statement; what he said was that he was arrested and was asked some questions. But there wasn't a signed statement, as far as I understand the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I haven't suggested there was a signed statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Or any statement, signed or unsigned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think "statement" may have a particular significance or understanding to the witness, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm going to be exploring that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Now, when you were at the CCIU and you were discussing matters with the CCIU, afterwards did you sign any documents about what you had told them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember about signing. I don't remember whether I signed or not, but I think I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: And when you were at the CCIU we understand that the statements that you gave there were of your own free will and truthful. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, maybe we did not mention everything because it was a very beginning, and we thought that they would take some steps in order to provide us with information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: You did mention to them in that statement your experiences on the 14th of June, 1998, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for those dates, I don't know exactly how I said that, but I gave the approximate of what happened. I don't remember the dates that I gave them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: By August 19th, 2001, had you spoken with - don't mention any names - had you spoken with any members of your family or other individuals concerning your experiences in the summer of 1998?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you could repeat the question, please. I didn't understand the first part.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: By August 19th, 2001, had you spoken with any members of your family or other individuals concerning your experiences in the summer of 1998?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I experienced, I did discuss it to certain extent; but for the event, how it actually happened, only two or three persons knew about it, not more.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: We should go into private session but for a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: When you spoke to the investigator at the CCIU on August 19th, 2001, you described what happened to you as you were walking down the road towards Zborce. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: You told the CCIU investigator that: "As I got closer I saw my uncle," and I won't mention any names, "and two masked UCK soldiers." True?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: That in fact was the same thing that you told us yesterday when being asked questions by Mr. Black. You said, and this is on page 11: "And there we found two masked people; they stopped us, too." Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Now, yesterday when we were talking about this incident you described the clothing that they were wearing. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I described that to some extent.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Well, yesterday you told us that one was dressed in a rather brownish reddish jacket and a pair of trousers and the other had a black jacket on and I think he trousers were rather darker. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: You indicated that they both had patches. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: And you identified who they were. You said --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Perhaps we should go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Well, sir, if you believed that you knew the identity of individuals in August of 2001 when you were speaking to the CCIU investigators and you were there, as you've told us, for the purpose of getting information and giving information so that you could track down what was going on, you certainly would have given the CCIU investigators those names, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, but I think I mentioned some names. I -- the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. fact is that these two persons, I guess that they were the persons I referred to when they first stopped us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: But you didn't mention their names to the CCIU investigator. That's what I'm driving at. In 2001, four years ago, you didn't mention these names.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I did say the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: During that self-same conference with the CCIU, you did mention the name of --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Perhaps it's private session, I'm not sure, so to make sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: And when you returned to Kosovo, did you again watch the news?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I followed the news again. I watched television again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: When the gentlemen who are on trial here were arrested, did you watch news concerning that arrest?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: You've told us that you have watched some of the proceedings here. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the proceedings here, but I saw when they were arrested.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Okay. Now, after they were arrested and during the trial proceedings that have been going on here, have you had a chance to watch any of the proceedings here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't watch.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: When you were in Kosovo after the war, did you read the newspaper?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Okay. What newspapers did you read, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember which ones. Maybe occasionally one. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Are there a lot of newspapers in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe there are, but I don't read much newspapers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Have you seen any of the gentlemen here sitting at this trial in this newspaper, their photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've seen Commander Celiku in -- on a newspaper.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Now, during the time that you were being interviewed by the people at the CCIU in August of 2001, were you shown any photographs at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Not of Celiku. I was shown some photographs, but I did not recognise any on those ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: I see. And when you had your meeting with the ICTY investigator in 2002, were you shown photographs at that time? And when I'm talking about photographs, I'm talking about photographs of people who may or may not have been responsible for what you suffered at Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: For those persons that I knew, I knew them as well last night. And for those that I didn't know, I said I didn't know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: So is your answer to my question then that you were shown photographs in 2002?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They showed me photographs. Those that I knew, I said I knew them; and those that I didn't, I didn't know them. There was several photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: The photographs that you were shown in 2002, were those single photographs or a bunch of photographs on a piece of paper together, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember what the order of the photographs was, but I said, I know this person, for the person that I knew. And I can't say that for someone that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: I understand. Do you recall as you sit here today any of the photographs that you identified in the interview in 2002?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even today those that I've seen whenever you want -- and if I remember I can tell you this person was there and this wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Perhaps my question was ill-framed. Maybe I'll try again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, could I just draw your attention to line 21. You may not have picked up the last words. I think you and the witness may be at cross-purposes as to which photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I appreciate the guidance. No, it's of great help.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: I want to go back now to your interview in November of 2002. All right? Are you with me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Good. During that interview do you remember if you were shown photographs of people who could have been guards or responsible for the mistreatment that you suffered?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, you've had an opportunity to speak with Mr. Black before you began testifying in these proceedings. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: When you spoke with Mr. Black, Mr. Black gave you a copy of the statements that you had previously made, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I see those statements, I can answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Let me ask you this question, sir: When you were with Mr. Black and you were preparing for your testimony here, did Mr. Black give you any pieces of paper to review?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read some, I don't know how many. If you could remind me, what is that piece of paper about?

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I can't, unfortunately, because I wasn't there so I'm going to have to rely on your memory with regard to this issue.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I read them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Would it be helpful, Your Honour, if he's shown the statements? I have them right here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, if in fact those the statements you gave to him, that would be helpful, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I think so. Perhaps he can answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Now, did you spend some time reviewing those statements before you came to court to testify?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whatever you asked me and if I remember and if that was true, I can tell you, I can answer your questions. I did not learn these statements by heart. I know what happened to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: I understand that. My simple question is: Did you spend some time reviewing those statements? That's all I'm asking you, not if you learned them by heart. But did you spend some time looking over them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He asked me questions, but I did not read through the statement. I really don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I've forgotten. When did you meet with Mr. Black? When was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Before you came to testify here. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Do you recall when you arrived in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Why?

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Is it -- I'm trying to help you in terms of time when you met with Mr. Black. Is the day you arrived in The Hague the day you met with Mr. Black?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I met with him here, not when I arrived in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Okay. And how many days ago was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It happened a day or two before. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Excellent. When you met with Mr. Black and he gave you the statements, did you have a chance to talk to an interpreter about the statements to -- so you could give Mr. Black some information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: And the discussion that you had with Mr. Black, was the interpreter that you were using, there were no difficulties there, were there? You understood each other pretty easily, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my recollection I read these statements up to certain points, but there was even no need for me to read because I cannot forget the things that happened. I gave the statement the way things happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Well, is it fair to say then that after you glanced over the statements you made a determination that you didn't need to look at them so you did not review the statements? Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ask me whatever you want about what is written in those statements and I can provide you with an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Well, I appreciate that, and I'm trying to just find out how you approached your preparation here and what information you reviewed. So if you could be of a little help here, that would be great. And as I understand it you glanced over the statements and then made a decision that this was information that you did not need. Is that a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whatever he asked me, I did give my answer to his question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: And did he ask you specific questions about your statements?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He asked me how it was, how it happened, how I gave my statements, and I will never change what I've said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: So, for example, would it be fair to say that he asked you the following: Is it true that what you said about Shala is that he was 45 to 50 years old, 1.8 metres tall, very thin, moustache, short black with grey hair. Is that what he asked you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what I stated in my statements, and I can still state it. That's the way it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: I understand that, and that's perfect. But my question is: Is that the kind of question that he asked you? He asked you a specific question, for example, about the description of Shala. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Guy-Smith. Mr. Topolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: I just have four things I want to ask you about. First of all, I'd like to give you a map, and I'd like you to use that ELMO next to you with a pointer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Could the witness please have P1, map 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Sir, if you take the pointer, please, and help us. You have told us very clearly that it was on the 14th of June, 1998, that you were taken prisoner. That's correct, is it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. As best you can using the pointer, could you show us on the map where you were when the two men stopped you and took you into their custody.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know maps very well and I cannot show it to you in the map. I can read these names here, Carraleve, but I cannot tell you on the map. I know that I was in the Carraleve territory at the part where Carraleve and Zborce separate. For something that I don't know, I will just say I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Does it mean then that when you were on your search for your relative at the moment you were taken prisoner, you were somewhere between Carraleve and Zborce. Is that the position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You don't need the map again. Before I go on I'd been asked by the gentleman who I think was just asking you some questions to ask you one that he omitted to ask you, so I do it on his behalf.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Pleasure, and there's no charge for this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: How tall are you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1.7 metres, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Back to the 14th of June when the two men took you into their custody somewhere between Carraleve and Zborce. Doing the best you can, can you tell us approximately what time of day this would have been?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately it was around 10.00 or 11.00. I can't say exactly what time it was, but it was before noon.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: One more question regarding this aspect. If you from that spot drove to the village of Dulje, approximately how long do you think that journey would take?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From there to Dulje it could be around 5 kilometres or 6. I didn't measure it in kilometres. Approximately. From my village to Dulje, it's about 10 minutes, not more. The journey is no longer than ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The second thing I want to ask you about is this: You have told us that after your release you were arrested by Serb authorities.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: I want to ask you one or two questions about that you've not been asked already. I know you'll be patient with me. And the first question is this: Were you taken to a police station by the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They caught me in a village, placed me in a car, and took me to the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Where was the police station they took you to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lipjan.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Approximately - again, doing the best you can - how long after you were released from custody, from Lapusnik I mean, how long was it after that that you were arrested and taken to a police station in Lipjan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be three or four months. I don't know for sure. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: I think you'll be able to answer my next question either yes or no, and I'm going to be very careful not to mention names. When you were taken to the police station in Lipjan, did you know that two members of your family had also been taken to a police station in Lipjan and interviewed by the Serbs? Did you know that, please yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know about this. I didn't know that at that time and I don't know it today.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to help you, and in order for me to do that properly so you can assist this Court, I'd like to go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Have you ever heard the name Srba Vujinovic an SUP police officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Are you absolutely sure about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am sure. I was never interested in him and I never dealt with such things.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Again, we are in open session and I shall be careful and I want you to be careful not to mention names. In relation to that gentleman whose name I've just given you, are you aware whether any members of your family have any connection or contact with that gentleman in 1998? In other words, have you heard members of your family talking about that man in 1998?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: This is not true. They never talked about him. Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't have any conversation about this subject you're mentioning. And to my knowledge, I don't remember us having to deal with them at any time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'll move on to the third thing I wanted to ask you about. But before I do that there's one more question about your dealings with the Serbs. Wait for the question. Wait for the question. In answer to the gentleman who was just asking you questions a few moments ago, you said to us page 16, line 4 to be exact: "They," that is the Serbs, "asked me to come the following day and give a statement." Do you remember the Serbs asking you to come back the following -- just wait for the question. I promise you you'll have all the time you need. Do you remember the Serbs asking you to come back and make a statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will tell you that way. When I was captured, I was captured by an Albanian policeman from Godance who was together with another Serb. These two persons are the ones who interrogated me and who beat me. The policeman was from Godance and his name was Fatmir; I don't know his last name. There was another Serb with him, and I don't know his name either. The name you mentioned, I don't remember that name. I never learnt his name because I didn't need it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Well, sir, that's a very interesting answer, but I'm afraid it's not an answer to the question I asked you. And I'll repeat the question I asked you, which was: Do you remember the Serbs asking you to come back and make a statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They said so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you go back and make a statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I didn't go. The following day I left for Germany.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: I now understand entirely your evidence on that. Thank you for your help. Last topic, and we need to go into -- I haven't asked you anything --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to finish this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: All right. If you want to say something else, I'm sure you can.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everybody knows about the incident when the police caught me, and they all know that the following day I left for Germany at 5.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. We now know that, too. I want to ask you just one more thing, and for it we need to go into private session at the beginning, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Last thing I want to ask you about, sir, and thank you for your patience. I want to ask you a couple of questions about the man Murrizi. Did you ever discover Murrizi's real name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for Murrizi's name and about Shala's, he said that as for Murrizi's name he thought it was Agim Murtezi. I think that's what he said about Murrizi's name.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Are you telling us that Shala told you Murrizi's real name was Agim Murtezi? Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: When either in Kosovo or Germany, I don't -- it doesn't matter where, when men arrived at this court here in The Hague, that was on television. Did you see any television broadcasts of defendants arriving at this court?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw that on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: You will have seen a man in this court whose name was Agim Murtezi. You saw him on the television, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how it was. To my recollection, that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you pick up a telephone and tell anyone that they had the wrong man, that that was not Murrizi from the camp? Did you tell anyone that, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. Not to a soul. I just saw that that person was not Murrizi. I didn't make any phone calls.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: That's all I ask you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Topolski. Yes, Mr. Black.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Just a few questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Witness, over the course of yesterday and today many times you've mentioned a person named Shala and you've talked to us about him. Now, what you've told us, was that on the basis of what you saw and experienced or was it on the basis of what other people told you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whatever I said about Shala, the truth is that I base it on what I saw. I saw him with my own eyes, Shala.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And when you pointed out Shala in the courtroom here yesterday, did you do that based on your own knowledge or based on what other people had told you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already stated in the statement. I can state it everywhere that I -- this person I cannot forget. He was there on the spot; he had the keys.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: You've also told us about a person named Qerqiz. Now, the things that you've told us, were they based on your personal knowledge or were they based on what other people had told you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard Shala calling him Qerqiz. That's where I heard the name mentioned. And when Emin Emini told me he said, This guy is from Racak. When they took him to that place, I don't know where they beat him, this is what he said to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And did you yourself see Qerqiz in Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have seen him masked.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And what about Commander Celiku? Did you yourself see him in Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have seen him without wearing a mask.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: When you pointed out Commander Celiku in the courtroom yesterday, did you do that based on your own knowledge or what other people had told you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-10 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I know this myself. I've seen him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Sir, you'll be pleased to know that that is the end of your evidence. The questioning had finished. Thank you for your attendance here and you are now free to go back to your home. You can leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, we had hoped to have the next witness available to start testifying -- start his testimony today. However, we've had some difficulties in the scheduling, so our next witness will not be available to Monday afternoon, the next session. So we do not have another witness for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We will need then to adjourn until 2.15 on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 7th day of February, 2005, at 2.15 p.m. 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 11.47 a.m.,
